dossier.public_summary: The dip changes dramatically from sector to sector and from transit to transit, with a few very deep events in two sectors driving the signal. A steady planet would look the same everywhere, so the variation points to stellar variability or a blended background eclipse rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Depth is not a calibration offset — it changes within the same SPOC 2-min product and from near-zero or negative to >1000 ppm between sectors, inconsistent with a planet of fixed size on the target. True astrophysical depth change favours a spot/variability or blend with sector-dependent dilution over a planet.

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent; the signal is carried by four deep outliers in two early sectors. This is positive evidence for a few bad/spot events or a blended deep eclipse appearing only sometimes, not a steady planetary transit.
reasons.value: p_consistent=3.195611240708241e-100, chi2=575.2602646297004 dof 33, share_of_top_3=0.801, outliers 1601 ppm (14.0 sigma), 1393 ppm (12.1 sigma), 1041 ppm (8.2 sigma), 795 ppm (6.2 sigma)

reasons.why: The formally significant sector-to-sector and transit-to-transit changes plus a marginal secondary near phase 0.367, while not definitive for an EB alone, support an astrophysical non-planet origin when combined with the above inconsistencies. Rank 0.08 matches only 8% of known planets and is expected for false positives showing these changes.
